title: Oversized MoE Runtime: Qwen3-Next-80B (48.4 GB) on a 16 GB M1 Mac, CPU-only
body:
I’ve been experimenting with running sparse MoE GGUF models whose total size is much larger than physical RAM.

The result is **Oversized MoE Runtime**, a small runtime/policy layer on top of `llama.cpp`.

The largest configuration I’ve validated so far:

    Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct Q4_K_M
    GGUF size:             48.41 GB
    Physical RAM:          16 GiB
    Hardware:              MacBook Air M1
    Backend:               CPU-only
    Metal:                 OFF
    Experts/layer:         512
    Active experts/token:  10

The basic idea is simple: keep the model mmap-backed and maintain a bounded **zero-copy residency set** for frequently reused expert pages, instead of trying to keep the full model resident.

In one matched Qwen3-Next-80B decode experiment:

    baseline:           3.39 tok/s
    residency quota32:  4.80 tok/s
    improvement:        +41.6%

Expert routing showed substantial temporal locality as well: LRU32 hit rates were roughly **56–64%** across measured workloads.

Interestingly, a larger cache was not automatically faster:

    LRU32: 3.80 tok/s
    LRU64: 3.79 tok/s

So the optimization target seems to be the overall physical-memory behavior rather than maximum cache hit rate.

I also tested Qwen3-30B-A3B, where decode throughput increased from **5.79 tok/s to 8.81 tok/s** with a residency quota of 48 experts/tensor.

v0.1 currently provides:

- `oversized-moe probe`
- `oversized-moe run`
- `oversized-moe serve`
- automatic RAM-aware residency policy
- runtime safety validation
- `qwen3moe` and `qwen3next` support
- 7 regression/smoke tests
- reproducible source release + patch series

Local completion and `llama-server` have both been validated, including an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` request.

**Project:**  
https://github.com/dimitripavlov/oversized-moe-runtime

**Benchmarks:**  
https://github.com/dimitripavlov/oversized-moe-runtime/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md

**v0.1 release:**  
https://github.com/dimitripavlov/oversized-moe-runtime/releases/tag/oversized-moe-v0.1

I’d be especially interested in feedback on the engine boundary: whether the mmap/prefetch control and bounded expert residency would make sense as more generic `llama.cpp` mechanisms rather than product-specific behavior.
